title: Choose the visual world for the listing page
question: The roll assigned The Datasheet. Keep it, take the pick or an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Datasheet
options.thesis: A private repo sold the way an engineer buys a part: every spec disclosed on one dense sheet, then an ordering block.
options.viewport: Part-number header (pbakaus / impeccable · Rev 4.1.2) across the top. Left: FEATURES as computed facts (3,537 files · 87.5 MB · Apache-2.0 · scan pass), DESCRIPTION from the README, then CONTENTS (file tree), DEPENDENCIES, REVISION HISTORY (release log). Right rail: ORDERING INFORMATION with price, update price and one order line, and ABSOLUTE MAXIMUM RATINGS (scan, size caps). Owned state: your revision printed solid in the history table, later revisions dashed, changed files bright and unchanged files ghosted, the order line reading UPDATE TO 4.1.2 · $3.
options.risk: Reads like a PDF if the type is set at datasheet size; the sheet must be tabular in structure but sized and spaced for a screen.

raised.raise: Owned state: what you already have prints ghosted, what the update adds prints bright, so the diff is read before it is paid for.
Revision history: the revision you own is the solid line, every other revision is dashed.
One red on the whole sheet, reserved for a failed scan; price and the order line never borrow it.
One imperative per sheet: a single order line, GET 4.1.2 · $9, and nothing else asks for a click.
Every computed number carries its provenance: computed-at and analyzer version in the table footers.
Total commitment to the ink set: three greys and one red, no tints, no gradients, no shadows.

options.label: The Long Listing
options.thesis: The manifest is literally the listing: mode, size, date, path, in columns, and the price is the last line.
options.viewport: A single monospace column listing that scrolls: header line with repo and version, then every path with its size and blob date, README rendered inline as a heredoc, dependencies as a second listing, release log as git log --oneline, and a final prompt line: $ pay 9.00 USDC.
options.risk: The most familiar destination for a developer tool; many runs in this category land on a terminal look, and it can read as a costume if the columns are not real.

regions.label: long listing · mode size date path

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: The repo as a numbered build: an inventory of parts up front, each release a step that adds bright pieces to a ghosted assembly.
options.viewport: Parts inventory (file inventory by kind) in a cornered box, then release steps in sequence, the newest step's added files bright red against the ghosted prior tree, the order button as the bag number.
options.case: Holds audience identification: developers recognise it instantly and the ghosted-prior / bright-new grammar is exactly the update state. Loses product clarity: a listing page needs prose and tables, and wordless arrows cannot carry a README or a licence.
options.risk: Playful register can undercut a $9 purchase decision and the sky-blue ground fights dense text.

regions.label: assembly · ghosted prior tree, new files bright

options.label: Pattern Envelope
options.thesis: Views A/B/C as versions, nested size lines as releases.
options.viewport: Envelope front indexes versions; the chosen one prints solid.
options.case: Developers do not identify with dressmaking, and the tissue metaphor obscures a file tree.
options.kept: The chosen size solid, every other size dashed.
options.risk: Reads as craft-fair whimsy on a purchase page.

options.label: VU Meter Bridge
options.thesis: Releases as a row of identical meters read at a sweep.
options.viewport: A row of meters, one per release, needles resting.
options.case: There is no live signal on a listing page; the meters would be decoration, and audiences do not identify a repo with a mixing desk.
options.kept: The arc past zero is the only red the instrument allows.
options.risk: Pure ornament without a signal to drive it.

options.label: Risograph System
options.thesis: Two spot inks misregistered over paper.
options.viewport: Cut-paper blocks in two inks; hover shudders the registration.
options.case: Misregistration destroys legibility in exactly the dense tables this page is made of; identification with developers is incidental.
options.kept: Total commitment to a small ink set.
options.risk: Decorative noise on a disclosure surface.

options.label: Treasure Map
options.thesis: Navigation as inference across an aged chart.
options.viewport: A chart with a faint red route rising under light.
options.case: The product's whole point is that nothing is hidden; a map that rewards inference contradicts disclosure.
options.risk: Theme-park register, and it argues against the product.

options.label: WPA Park Poster
options.thesis: Stacked flat planes and one imperative caption.
options.viewport: A flattened scene above a one-word imperative.
options.case: A poster carries one sentence; the listing page carries three thousand file paths.
options.risk: Nothing on the page to render as a landscape.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A package-registry product page: title, sidebar stats, tabs, a primary button.
canonCard.viewport: Repo title and description, README tab, stats sidebar with an install/buy button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from GitHub and npm by design.
